editorial.headline: Metal Objects at the Edge of the Catalogue
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25999 covers the miscellaneous metal products that do not sit neatly in a narrower manufacturing class, with full national foreign ownership but a scope-sensitive Bali pathway.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25999 is the workshop of remaining metal goods: the activity code for making metal products that are real, manufactured, and commercially specific, but not classified elsewhere in a narrower group. The record points to small everyday articles such as hair clips, safety pins, staples, paper clips, sewing, knitting, and embroidery needles, buckle heads, metal chains, bells, picture frames, metal nameplates, non-electric metal signs, badges, metal hair curlers and combs, and umbrella frames or handles. It also reaches into heavier or more technical products: propellers, ship chains, ship anchors, installed railway fixtures, woven metal cable coverings, certain non-conductor metal cables, sealing rings, screw-machine products, foil pouches, permanent metal magnets, and vacuum metal bottles or jugs.

That range is the point of the code. It is not a prestige label for one product line, and it is not a catch-all for anything vaguely metallic. It is for manufacturers whose output is a finished or semi-finished metal article within this residual metal-products field. A founder using this classification should be able to describe the actual item being made with care, because the record itself is broad: a paper clip, an anchor, a metal badge, and a vacuum metal jug all sit inside the same recorded scope. The boundary also matters: the record expressly leaves sewing-machine needles outside this activity.

On business scale, the national record is expansive. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale operators, so it is not reserved in the record for only cottage production or only large industrial plants. At the national level, PMA status remains TERBUKA, while foreign ownership may reach 100%. In plain terms, the national investment line treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling, with the source recorded as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali is more delicate. The record does not mark this code as automatically blocked, but it does mark the Bali status as Blocked (scope-dependent). The reason given is precise: OSS risk at scale Besar is low on some scopes but higher on others, and PMA registration in Bali is registrable only by declaring the higher-risk scope; the exact activity must be verified live in OSS. This sits under the recorded Bali moratorium rule that Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. The honest reading is therefore not that KBLI 25999 is simply closed in Bali, and not that it is casually open either. Nationally it is fully open; in Bali, the registrability of a PMA filing depends on the exact declared metal-product activity and its OSS risk treatment.
